beats.name: Beat 1: The Artist and the Studio

children.notes: Introductory remarks trimmed to fit the opening transition into the studio.

cards.text: Viviana talking about how being a full-time artist is hard work but a dream.
Under the entrance b-roll, overlap Viviana’s voiceover introducing herself, her background, and Mud Witch.

Open on-camera with Viviana sharing what it means to be a full-time creative artist. Immediately cut to b-roll of her walking along the street into the studio, establishing the transition into her working environment. Cut briefly to the studio shelf to establish her brand identity.
Viviana walking into the studio entrance from the sidewalk.

cards.notes: Sign insert shot trimmed for a quick studio establishment.

cards.text: The Mud Witch sign sitting on the studio shelf.
Welcoming and grounded; sets an authentic, personal tone for her pottery practice.

beats.name: Beat 2: Mud Witch Style & Body Positivity

cards.text: Viviana explaining how learning clay merged with the body positivity movement.
Interview voiceover continues over the b-roll, explaining the creation of the Chubby and Venus shapes inspired by diverse bodies.

Return to an on-camera interview where Viviana explains how discovering the body positivity movement shaped the distinctive silhouette of her pottery. As she speaks about chubby forms and abstract representations of bodies, cut away to show her early wheel-throwing process alternated with shots of unglazed inventory waiting on studio shelves.

children.notes: Wheel-throwing footage trimmed to match the discussion of forming shapes.
B-roll of unfinished inventory trimmed to cut to next beat cleanly.

cards.text: Viviana shaping a clay pot on the pottery wheel.
Stacks of unpainted, raw ceramic pieces sitting on studio shelving.
Inspiring and creative; highlights the intentionality and playfulness behind her distinct designs.

beats.name: Beat 3: The Artist's Hand and Human Connection

cards.text: Viviana’s voiceover explains the concept of the "artist's hand" and how handmade pottery reconnects people in a disconnected society through touch.

cards.notes: Concluding thoughts trimmed slightly to conclude the piece with emotional punch.

cards.text: Follow with her concluding thoughts on the necessity of physical mediums and human interaction.

Explore why handmade ceramics hold emotional value. Alternate between Viviana refining pieces across various production stages and checking unfinished work on the shelves, culminating in a dedicated close shot of her working at the wheel.

children.notes: Painting shot cut to establish hand-crafting process.
Inspection shot trimmed to transition into final wheel work.

cards.text: Viviana holding and painting a ceramic bowl.
Viviana inspecting unfinished pottery pieces on a studio shelf.

cards.notes: Closing wheel shot trimmed to hold through the end of the voiceover.

cards.text: Viviana focused at the wheel, expertly shaping clay using pottery tools.
Reflective, tactile, and meaningful; ends on the tactile artistry of pottery and the human warmth it brings.

meta.brief: Plan a ~60-second documentary about how Viviana turned her pottery into Mud Witch and why she values pottery.
meta.guidance:
- begin with a short soundbite of her talking about being artist, then go into discussion of her body positivity inspired style. end with her talking about  building handmade ceramics and how it connects people. throughout, use clips of her focused and working on different stages of the pottery-making process alternating with b-roll clips of her unfinished inventory. end with a clip of her working.

requirements
- start with a clip of her talking about being an artist
- immediately follow with her walking into the studio, overlapped with audio of her introducing herself
- have three b-roll clips of her working on her stuff with interview audio
- have two clips of her talking in interview

meta.brief: Plan a ~60-second documentary about how Viviana turned her pottery into Mud Witch and why she values pottery.
meta.guidance:
- begin with a short soundbite of her talking about being artist, then go into discussion of her body positivity inspired style. end with her talking about  building handmade ceramics and how it connects people. throughout, use clips of her focused and working on different stages of the pottery-making process alternating with b-roll clips of her unfinished inventory. end with a clip of her working.

requirements
- start with a clip of her talking about being an artist
- immediately follow with her walking into the studio, overlapped with audio of her introducing herself
- have three b-roll clips of her working on her stuff with interview audio
- have two clips of her talking in interview
